home.title: Optimize a CATIA tree
home.subtitle: Reorganize a file structure from exported data — no CATIA required, no file moved.
home.step1: Import: scan a local folder (metadata only) or import a CSV / JSON listing.
home.step2: Tree: review metrics (depth, fan-out, duplicates, naming).
home.step3: Suggestions: generate the plan (heuristics + Mistral), then accept / reject.
home.step4: Export: download the CSV plan and the .bat / .sh script, to run yourself.

conversion.title: CATIA 3D → Composer conversion
conversion.subtitle: Conversion plan (dry-run).
conversion.dryRun: Generates a mapping + a reviewable Python (win32com) script driving Composer (DRY_RUN by default). No conversion is run by the app.
conversion.workflow1: Import the source to convert: a folder (or a file selection) or a .zip archive.
conversion.workflow3: Generate the plan: all files are listed, known CAD formats are pre-selected.
conversion.workflow4: Check / uncheck the files to convert (uncheck anomalies).
conversion.workflow5: Export the Python script (Composer / win32com) and the plan CSV.
conversion.workflowScriptNote: The app does NOT convert by itself: it generates a reviewable Python script (win32com, DRY_RUN=True by default) + a CSV. You review the script, set DRY_RUN=False, then run it yourself.
conversion.sourceBanner: Import a whole folder (local) or a .zip archive. All convertible files are listed; deselect the ones to skip.
conversion.sourceRequired: Import a folder or a .zip above.
conversion.outputInfo: Flat output: SMGXML + SMGG at the root, the rest moved to "_autres/". Non-destructive: nothing is deleted, your source files are never modified.
conversion.execHint: Runs the script on this PC. "Test" simulates (dry-run, does not call Composer). "Run" drives Composer for real (Composer + pywin32 required). Non-destructive: creates output files, never touches sources.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Mistral API key and models in use.
settings.apiKeyStored: A key is already stored (leave blank to keep it).
settings.onedriveNotice: OneDrive is read via its locally synced folder (no cloud connection). The input is the common navigation root (e.g. the SAFRAN folder): broad, each step then picks its own subfolder / file under it. The output receives generated deliverables (CSV plans, scripts).
settings.composerNotice: CATIA → Composer conversion requires an active license. Enter your floating license server (DSLS) here: the generated conversion script sets it in the environment before driving Composer. If empty, your machine's local license is used.
settings.composerHint: Best-effort: the exact variable read by your Composer edition is still to be confirmed (candidates DSLICSRV / DS_LICENSE_SERVER / LSERVRC).
settings.llmHint: When disabled, AI-driven tasks are skipped (deterministic result). The key is kept.

identification.nomenBanner: Path under the Source root (Settings tab). Identifies the CATParts to process + the mono-color SINs.
identification.previewHint: Load the preview, then configure the mapping to enable analysis.
identification.mappingTitle: Column mapping (at least one identity: SIN or PN)
identification.identityRequired: Map at least one identity column: SIN, OLD P/N or NEW P/N.
identification.monoBanner: Pick the Materials sheet, the identity column (to link back to parts), a number of slot columns, then map them. A part is mono-body when its filled slots share a single distinct value.
identification.monoRequired: Map the identity column and at least one slot.

smgxmlRecolor.title: Apply color in the SMGXML
smgxmlRecolor.banner: Step 3. Sets the style (Color Ref → Actor.Style, texture applied by Composer from the C: library) and/or the RGB color (SCLIT > Neutral > Actor.Color) of the nomenclature parts. Dry-run by default; applying writes the file keeping a .bak.
smgxmlRecolor.refBanner: Maps each nomenclature "Color Ref" (e.g. Visserie) to an RGB, then written into SCLIT > Neutral > Actor.Color. Falls back to the nomenclature mono color otherwise.
smgxmlRecolor.textureBanner: The style name (Color Ref) written into Actor.Style points to a file in the library, suffixed with the extension (.SMGStyleSet). Set the library path so the SMGXML references it directly.

smgxmlRename.title: Rename parts in the SMGXML
smgxmlRename.banner: Step 4. Replaces the old part name with the new one (attributes + references). Dry-run by default; applying writes the file keeping a .bak.
smgxmlRename.mappingRequired: Add at least one old=new mapping.

qc.title: Quality Control checklist
qc.banner: Step 5. Verification of parts in the assembly, review-style. Tick OK / KO / N/A and comment each point.

data.resetBanner: Irreversible operation. The Mistral configuration (app_config table) is preserved.

architecture.title: Backend ↔ Frontend in 30 seconds
architecture.backendDesc: Python 3.11+ · FastAPI under /api/v1/ · Pydantic v2 · SQLAlchemy 2 + SQLite + Alembic · structlog JSON + X-Request-Id. Mistral via httpx async (chat streaming SSE) + sync (embeddings). No Mistral SDK.
architecture.frontendDesc: React + Vite app (TS strict, Tailwind, RHF + Zod, i18next, Zustand, TanStack Query) with @internal/ui and @internal/design-tokens, served by the backend. Consumes the REST API directly.
architecture.step1: Settings tab → enter the Mistral key (stored in SQLite, app_config table).
architecture.step2: Test the connection - lists the available Mistral models.
architecture.step3: Data tab → view the counters and reset tables if needed.
architecture.step4: Follow the 5-step pipeline: Identification → Preparation → Processing → Integration → Control.
